question: What primary body system does an intravenous pyelogram evaluate?
explanation: An IVP is specifically designed to image the kidneys, ureters, and bladder using a radiopaque contrast dye. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why is a contrast medium injected intravenously during an IVP?

options.A: To highlight urinary structures on X-rays
options.B: To prevent infection during the procedure
options.C: To flush out small kidney stones completely
options.D: To numb the urinary tract structures

explanation: The radiopaque dye is filtered by the kidneys and makes the internal urinary tract visible on X-ray imaging. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h1)

question: A common clinical indication for performing an IVP is...
explanation: IVP is frequently used to locate kidney stones and assess urinary tract obstructions. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h2)

question: How does an IVP help a patient with recurrent urinary tract infections?

options.A: It measures the exact daily fluid intake
options.B: It kills bacteria hiding in the bladder
options.C: It strengthens the detrusor muscle tone

explanation: Structural anomalies cause urine stasis, which leads to frequent infections that an IVP can help visualize. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h2)

question: Which condition is an absolute contraindication for an IVP procedure?
explanation: Patients with a known iodine allergy are at high risk for severe anaphylaxis when exposed to contrast dye. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h3)

question: Why must metformin be withheld from patients receiving iodinated contrast media?

options.A: It stops the contrast dye from working
options.B: It increases the risk of lactic acidosis
options.D: It lowers the blood pressure too quickly

explanation: If renal function drops after contrast administration, metformin accumulates and can lead to dangerous lactic acidosis. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h3)

question: What is the primary reason for administering a laxative before an IVP?

options.A: To stimulate rapid urine production by the kidneys
options.B: To relax the abdominal wall muscles fully
options.D: To clear fecal matter that obscures imaging

explanation: Stool and gas in the bowel block clear views of the kidneys and ureters on the X-ray plates. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h4)

question: A patient scheduled for an IVP asks why they must empty their bladder right before the test starts. The best nursing response is...

options.A: To make it easier to insert the intravenous line
options.B: To provide a fresh urine sample for laboratory testing
options.C: To prevent accidental leakage during the procedure
options.D: To obtain an accurate baseline image before dye is given

explanation: An empty bladder allows the initial scout film to clearly show baseline anatomical structures without urine interference. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h4)

question: What is the purpose of the initial scout film taken during an IVP?

options.A: To check bowel prep and find existing stones
options.B: To numb the skin before needle insertion
options.C: To test the patient for iodine allergies
options.D: To measure the exact volume of the bladder

explanation: The scout film confirms the bowel is clean and identifies any stones visible before dye administration. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h5)

question: Why are abdominal compression bands sometimes used during an IVP procedure?

options.A: To keep the patient safely positioned on the table
options.B: To prevent the contrast dye from reaching the bladder
options.C: To stimulate peristalsis and clear remaining bowel gas
options.D: To slow down urine flow and enhance system filling

explanation: Compression over the lower ureters temporarily holds urine in the kidneys to make the collecting system clearer. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h5)

question: A normal sensation a patient may report during the intravenous contrast injection is...

options.A: A warm flushing feeling and metallic taste
options.C: Severe sharp pain in the lower back
options.D: Sudden numbness in both lower limbs

explanation: Patients commonly experience a temporary warm flush and a strange taste immediately after contrast enters the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h6)

question: Why is encouraging high fluid intake important immediately after an IVP?

options.B: To help flush out the contrast dye
options.D: To keep the bladder muscle stretched

explanation: Abundant fluids promote rapid diuresis, clearing the nephrotoxic contrast medium from the kidneys. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h6)

question: Which symptom indicates a severe, life-threatening reaction to contrast media?

options.C: Mild metallic taste in the mouth

explanation: Airway swelling and breathing difficulty are signs of severe anaphylaxis requiring immediate emergency care. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h7)

question: A patient develops hives and shortness of breath during contrast injection. What is the immediate nursing action?

options.A: Send the patient back to the ward
options.B: Ask the patient to take slow, deep breaths
options.D: Wait to see if the symptoms clear up

explanation: Stopping the trigger is the first step in managing any acute adverse drug reaction. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h7)

question: What does a filling defect observed on an IVP film typically suggest?
explanation: A filling defect represents a mass or stone taking up space and blocking the normal flow of contrast dye. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h8)

question: How does hydronephrosis present on an IVP image?

options.C: Dilation of the renal pelvis and calyces
options.D: Complete absence of the urinary bladder

explanation: Obstruction causes urine to back up, leading to noticeable swelling and enlargement of the renal collecting system. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h8)
